security_audit.summary: Most markdown backtick and localhost findings are false positives because they are local Playwright examples. The real risks are command execution in scripts/with_server.py and instructions that discourage source review before execution. The author should remove black-box execution guidance and harden process launching.

remediation.issue: The server helper starts user-supplied commands with shell=True.
remediation.suggestion: Accept argument lists or trusted presets, and require explicit approval before running local shell commands.

remediation.issue: The documentation tells agents not to read helper source before execution.
remediation.suggestion: Remove black-box execution guidance and require source review before running bundled scripts.

remediation.issue: Examples write logs and screenshots to fixed output paths.
remediation.suggestion: Document these writes and allow configurable output paths to prevent accidental overwrites.

remediation.issue: Examples use fixed localhost URLs and ports.
remediation.suggestion: Make the target URL configurable and state that network access should stay local by default.

content.user_title: Test Local Web Apps with Playwright
content.value_statement: Frontend behavior is hard to verify when dynamic pages hide selectors and browser errors. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through local Playwright tests, screenshots, DOM inspection, console logs, and server setup.
actual_capabilities: Provides a decision tree for static HTML, existing servers, and managed local servers.
Shows headless Chromium testing with Python Playwright.
Includes a helper that starts servers, waits for ports, runs a command, and cleans up.
Demonstrates discovery of buttons, links, inputs, and rendered DOM state.
Demonstrates screenshot capture and console log collection during browser automation.
limitations: Focused on local web applications and static HTML, not remote site monitoring.
Requires Python Playwright and browser dependencies to be installed.
The server helper executes local commands, so users must review commands before use.
Examples use fixed localhost ports and output paths that may need adjustment.

use_cases.title: Verify a Local Feature
use_cases.description: Run a browser test against a local dev server and capture visible behavior.

use_cases.title: Debug UI Failures
use_cases.description: Inspect rendered buttons, links, inputs, screenshots, and console messages after a page loads.

use_cases.title: Automate Static HTML Checks
use_cases.description: Open a local HTML file, interact with controls, and capture before and after screenshots.

prompt_templates.title: Open a Local Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check for a running local app.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to open my local app at the current dev server URL. Wait for the page to finish loading and report visible issues.

prompt_templates.title: Find Interactive Elements
prompt_templates.scenario: Discover selectors before writing a test.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Playwright to inspect the rendered page. List visible buttons, links, inputs, and likely selectors for the main workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Console Problems
prompt_templates.scenario: Debug browser errors during an interaction.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a local browser automation pass, capture console messages, perform the main user action, and summarize warnings or errors.

prompt_templates.title: Run with Managed Servers
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with one or more local servers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the server command with me, start the required local servers, run a Playwright workflow after ports are ready, and clean up processes.

output_examples.input: Check whether the dashboard page loads and shows expected navigation.
output_examples.output: A short test report with navigation status, discovered page elements, console warnings, and screenshot file names.

output_examples.input: Find selectors for the sign-up form in my local app.
output: Visible inputs for name and email were found.
The submit button was visible after the page reached a stable load state.
Suggested selectors were based on labels, roles, and stable IDs.

output_examples.input: Run a static HTML interaction and capture screenshots.
output_examples.output: A before and after summary describing the clicked control, filled fields, final page state, and saved screenshots.

best_practices: Review local server commands before running the helper script.
Wait for stable page loading before inspecting dynamic content.
Prefer role, label, text, or stable ID selectors over fragile layout selectors.
anti_patterns: Running unknown server commands without source review or user approval.
Inspecting dynamic pages before scripts and network activity settle.
Treating example localhost ports and output paths as universal defaults.

faq.question: Does this skill test remote production websites?
faq.answer: It is designed for local web applications and static HTML files. Remote testing should require explicit user approval.

faq.question: Which browser automation library does it use?
faq.answer: The examples use Python Playwright with headless Chromium.

faq.question: Can it start my development server?
faq.answer: Yes, the helper can start local servers and wait for ports. Review every command before execution.

faq.question: Can it capture screenshots?
faq.answer: Yes, the examples show full page screenshots for rendered pages and static HTML workflows.

faq.question: Can it collect browser console logs?
faq.answer: Yes, the console logging example captures browser console messages during a Playwright session.

faq.question: Does it generate complete test suites?
faq.answer: No. It provides testing patterns and examples that can guide focused Playwright automation.
